title: Area (Counting Squares)
description: Learn area for Class 3 by counting unit squares. Find area of rectangles and compare areas of different shapes. Free online tests and IMO practice.

topics.title: Measure Area by Counting Unit Squares
topics.concept:
Area is the amount of flat surface inside a shape, measured in square units (e.g., cm², m²).

To find area:

  • Count the unit squares that fit inside the shape
  • For rectangles: Area = Length x Width

examples.problem: Rectangle 4 cm x 3 cm. Find the area.
examples.solution: Area = 4 x 3 = 12 cm². Count: 4 columns x 3 rows = 12 unit squares.

examples.problem: Square with side 5 cm. Find the area.
examples.solution: Area = 5 x 5 = 25 cm². 5 rows of 5 squares.

examples.problem: An irregular shape made of 8 full squares and 2 half-squares. Find the area.

recap: Area = number of unit squares inside a shape.
Units for area: cm², m², square units.

topics.title: Compare Area of Two Shapes
topics.concept:
To compare areas:

  1. Calculate each shape's area using Length x Width (or count squares)
  2. Compare the numbers
  3. Larger area = more space inside

Two shapes with the same area can look very different!

examples.problem: Which has larger area: a 3x5 rectangle or a 4x4 square?
examples.solution: Rectangle: 3x5=15 cm². Square: 4x4=16 cm². 16 > 15, so the square has larger area.

examples.problem: Compare shapes: one 2x6 (12 cm²), another 3x5 (15 cm²).
examples.solution: 3x5=15 cm² > 2x6=12 cm². The 3x5 shape has larger area.

examples.problem: Two shapes both have area 24 cm². Can they look different?
examples.solution: Yes! A 4x6 rectangle and a 3x8 rectangle both have area 24 cm² but look completely different.

recap: Calculate each area, then compare the numbers.
Same area does not mean same shape — different dimensions can give same area.

Two shapes with the same number of squares have:
Which is larger: $12$ squares or $9$ squares?
A $4$-by-$2$ shape and a $3$-by-$3$ shape: which is larger?

questions.explanation: 4x4=16 cm². 3x6=18 cm². 18>16, so 3x6 has more area.

questions.q: A shape has 10 full unit squares + 4 half-squares. Area = ?
Square area = 49 cm². What is each side?
questions.explanation: Side x side = 49. Since 7 x 7 = 49, side = 7 cm.

questions.q: Rectangle area = 24 cm², length = 6 cm. Width = ?
questions.explanation: Area = L x W. 24 = 6 x W. W = 24/6 = 4 cm.

questions.q: Shape A has 15 squares. Shape B has 20 squares. Difference in area = ?
A rectangle has area 36 cm². Give two possible pairs of side lengths.
options: All of the above pairs work
questions.explanation: 36 cm² can be made by 1x36, 2x18, 3x12, 4x9, 6x6. Multiple pairs work.

questions.q: A square has the same area as a 4 cm x 9 cm rectangle. What is the square's side?
questions.explanation: Rectangle area = 4x9 = 36 cm². Square side = sqrt(36) = 6 cm.

questions.q: A rectangle's area is 24 cm². If you double both length and width, what is the new area?
questions.explanation: If L and W are both doubled: new area = (2L)x(2W) = 4LW = 4x24 = 96 cm².

questions.q: A rectangle's length is twice its width. Area = 72 cm². Find the dimensions.
questions.explanation: Let W = width, L = 2W. L x W = 2W^2 = 72. W^2 = 36. W=6, L=12.

questions.q: Which has more area: 8 cm x 3 cm or 5 cm x 5 cm?
questions.explanation: 8x3=24 cm². 5x5=25 cm². 25>24, so 5x5 has more area.

questions.q: How many 2 cm x 3 cm tiles are needed to cover a 6 cm x 8 cm floor?
questions.explanation: Floor area = 6x8=48 cm². Tile area = 2x3=6 cm². Tiles needed = 48/6 = 8. Wait: 48/6=8. Answer is 8.
